note: Scenario-agnostic. Lives outside scenario JSON. Spec v1.0 §6. Career district (char.ray, char.dana, five scenes, two props, three vignettes) added without forking: one registry, two districts.
modesNote: 'none' is an INTENTIONAL blank: the node is a scene by presentation type but deliberately carries no artwork. It resolves to a null render block, the same shape 'messages' produces, and is set only through an explicit modeOverrides entry — never inferred from a missing visual block, which already means 'infer from location'. Added for the_instruction/escalate_bare, whose testPlaythrough declares the absence deliberate.

char.ray.name: Ray
char.ray.note: Ray Okonjo, manager. figure_c reuses figure_a's geometry contract only — basePoint, headSocket, neckSpan. Face, hair, proportion and wardrobe are drawn fresh. No rear figure: nothing in The Instruction frames over a shoulder and the player is never drawn.

char.dana.name: Dana
char.dana.note: Dana Whitfield, engagement lead. figure_d reuses figure_b's geometry contract only. Two registers because she appears in two nodes and one of them is an alternative to the other; a third would be an orphan under validator rule 8.

defaultWardrobeNote: resolve.py hard-coded 'home_casual' as the wardrobe floor, which no Career character has. Reading it per character removes fifteen otherwise-identical nodeOverrides. The two Neighbourhood entries restate the existing value, so The Secret's render blocks are unchanged.
scenesNote: resolve.py reads scene_def['default_time'] and offers no per-node override, so a room seen at two times is two scene tokens and two assets. desk_evening carries Act 1 (Wednesday, half past eight) and desk_day carries the Friday afternoon reply — the node the whole scenario resolves through.

vig.table_three.note: establish beat 3 — player POV, third glass in foreground (§11.2)

vig.call_without_you.note: ask2_refuse_response panel 1 — a Monday client call, seen from outside the room

vig.kitchen_pleasantry.note: ask2_refuse_response panel 2 — the break-out kitchen, two people, nobody asking what you're working on

vig.june_two_seats.note: ask2_refuse_response panel 3 — two seats taken on the June phase

propsNote: Two new props for the whole Career scenario. The prose places only two objects in a room and moves them between scenes; everything else the district needs is environment furniture, which the scene owns.
